review_scope: Approved after independent review of the corrected draft. Every material claim was re-asserted as an exact substring of fresh captures fetched 2026-10-28T11:32:45Z of the nine Cloudflare documentation and launch-post pages plus the project README and repository metadata; the two rework items (per-page last-updated dates, and the README ~$40 time unit) are corrected and re-checked. No managed-service test was run and none is claimed.

claims.note: Headline and description name the documented API, compaction lifecycle and beta boundary only; no measured result, ranking or price is asserted.
Frames the page as a documentation review: isolation unit, binding, methods and limits, with beta availability and unpublished price stated as open.
Each row maps to a linked reference page; the bottom four rows are explicitly marked vendor-described or not specified rather than presented as facts.
Binding block reproduces the documented wrangler.jsonc and wrangler.toml agent_memory entries: binding plus namespace, multiple entries for multiple namespaces.
Ten methods and both name-length limits (100 characters) come from the Workers API reference; the first-call penalty for profile creation is that page's own warning.
getProfile and its create-if-absent behaviour are the documented namespace method; the template string is illustrative code, not a service feature.
ingest() takes an array of messages with sessionId in the options argument and is documented as idempotent.
remember() takes content and optional sessionId only and returns the stored memory; the service-assigned type and summary are that page's wording.
recall() options (thinkingLevel, responseLength), list() filters and pagination, and the omission of content from list entries are documented on the Workers API page.
Batch-at-compaction guidance and the experimental agents/experimental/memory/session import both come from the get-started guide.
Content-addressed SHA-256 IDs truncated to 128 bits is the vendor's description of its ingestion pipeline in the launch post.
Chunking at roughly 10,000 characters, two-message overlap, four concurrent chunks, the 9+ message detail pass and the eight-check verifier are vendor-stated pipeline details.
The launch post names LongMemEval, LoCoMo and BEAM and publishes no result; the page asserts absence of a figure, not a performance claim.
Limit values are copied from the limits page and the Workers API limits table; no value is derived by testing.
Records a real inconsistency between two primary pages (list max 1,000 versus 500) and resolves it conservatively by advising the lower bound.
Arithmetic consequences of the documented caps (message count and byte size against a compaction event) given as guidance, with no measured size claim.
Not billed during beta and the at-least-30-days notice commitment are stated on the pricing page; no unit price exists there, hence cost is unknown rather than zero.
Exportability is a stated launch-post commitment while R2 export is future work and no export endpoint appears in the reference pages.
Design advice for an adapter boundary; the skeleton is labelled an implementation guide and explicitly not a benchmark of any service.
SQLite table with namespace, profile and session keys plus an FTS5 porter index mirrors the documented scoping model; illustrative code, not vendor code.
Schema encodes the documented namespace>profile>memory hierarchy locally; no platform behaviour is asserted.
128-bit truncated SHA-256 over session, role and content mirrors the vendor's documented content addressing; locally this is the author's reconstruction, not vendor code.
Supersede-with-pointer instead of delete mirrors the documented supersession semantics; the code is illustrative and was not measured.
recall() skeleton filters on namespace and profile and hides superseded rows, matching the documented isolation and supersession model; lexical channel only, as the code comment states.
Repository architecture, stack, routes and idempotency come from the README; the project is described as a reference implementation, not a maintained dependency.

The cost figures are quoted verbatim from the README section headed "Cost (1k users, 20 chats)" ("Luna ~$40. Cloudflare floor $5. DOs $0. Embeddings + Vectorize ~cents."). The source states no time unit, method or date, so the $40 is presented as the author's rough estimate, not a monthly bill, and explicitly not a measurement of this project or of the managed service.
Navigation links to four related pages in the same corpus; no factual claim about this service.

Discloses the method and limits of the check with the per-page last-updated dates actually read: index, concepts/namespaces-profiles, concepts/how-agent-memory-works and platform/pricing = Jun 2, 2026; api/workers-api and platform/limits = Jun 3, 2026; get-started = Oct 21, 2026; launch post datePublished 2026-04-17, dateModified 2026-07-15. The drift caveat is scoped to the June reference pages; the check ran locally on 2026-10-28, the captures are not redistributed, and no managed-service test was run.

numbers.note: Every number traces to a linked page: 500 messages, 32768 bytes, 1024 bytes, 64/100/32 character limits, list default 20 with the 500-versus-1000 disagreement recorded as a correction, 128-bit truncation, ~10000-character chunks, four concurrent chunks, nine-message detail threshold, five retrieval channels, eight verifier checks, 30-day notice. Nothing is author-measured.

model_ids.note: bge-m3 and the OpenRouter model are attributed to the thisuxhq README; no model version is invented and no capability claim is made for either.

pricing.note: The only managed-service pricing statements are "not billed during private beta" and the at-least-30-days notice, both from the pricing page; the README's $40 and $5 figures are quoted verbatim under its own heading "Cost (1k users, 20 chats)", which carries no time unit, method or date, so they are labelled the author's rough estimate and no monthly cost is asserted; managed-service cost is stated as unknown rather than zero.

dates_versions.note: Beta status, per-per-page documentation last-updated dates read on each page at 2026-10-28 11:32 UTC (index, concepts/namespaces-profiles, concepts/how-agent-memory-works, platform/pricing = 2026-06-02; api/workers-api, platform/limits = 2026-06-03; get-started = 2026-10-21), launch-post datePublished 2026-04-17 and dateModified 2026-07-15, the review date 2026-10-28 and the repository created/last-push dates are each stated with provenance. benchmarks.note: LongMemEval, LoCoMo and BEAM appear only as benchmarks the launch post names without publishing a result; the page states explicitly that no accuracy figure exists and ranks the service against nothing.

sponsorship.note: No paid placement, affiliate link or sponsored mention; the single third-party project appears as a reference implementation with its thin track record stated.
